Small helpers: parsing bibcodes, normalising document arguments, flattening.

This module duck-types documents and libraries instead of importing the models, so any module (including the models themselves) can import it without a cycle.

## scixplorer.utils.flatten

Written `utils.flatten` after `from scixplorer import *`.

```python
flatten(obj)
```

Flatten nested containers into one list, dropping `None`.

Lists, tuples, sets, dicts (their values) and iterators such as generators are expanded recursively. Everything else is kept as a single item, including strings and other iterables such as libraries or queries (so nothing is fetched from ADS). `None` is dropped at every level, so that `Document.affiliation` (one entry per author: an affiliation, a tuple of them, or `None`) can be scanned directly:

```python
any(aff.country == "Australia" for aff in flatten(doc.affiliation))
```

## scixplorer.utils.parse_bibcode

Written `utils.parse_bibcode` after `from scixplorer import *`.

```python
parse_bibcode(bibcode)
```

Split a bibcode into its parts, with the padding dots removed.

Returns a dict with keys `year`, `journal_abbreviation`, `volume`, `qualifier`, `page_number` and `first_letter_of_last_name`. A digit in the qualifier position is the leading digit of a five-digit page, so it is moved into `page_number` and `qualifier` is `""`:

```python
>>> parse_bibcode("1996PhRvB..5411169K")["page_number"]
'11169'
```

Raises `ValueError` if `bibcode` is not a 19-character bibcode.

## scixplorer.utils.to_bibcodes

Written `utils.to_bibcodes` after `from scixplorer import *`.

```python
to_bibcodes(*items)
```

Collect the bibcodes of everything given, in order, without duplicates.

Each item may be a bibcode string (surrounding whitespace is removed), an object with a `bibcode` attribute (a document), an object with a `bibcodes` attribute holding strings (a library: its list of bibcodes is used, without fetching each document), or any other iterable of these (lists, sets, generators, queries), nested to any depth. Bibcodes are not checked against a pattern, because ADS also accepts other identifiers; the server decides what is valid.

Raises `ValueError` for an empty string or a document whose `bibcode` is `None`, and `TypeError` for anything else.
